question.text: Two spheres $\mathrm{S}_1$ and $\mathrm{S}_2$ of masses $\mathrm{m}_1$ and $\mathrm{m}_2$ respectively collide with each other. Initially $\mathrm{S}_1$ is at rest and $\mathrm{S}_2$ is movingwith velocity v along x -axis. After collision $\mathrm{S}_2$ has a velocity $\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2}$ in a direction perpendicular to the original direction. The sphere $\mathrm{S}_1$ moves after collision

options.text: with a velocity in the direction $\theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)$ to the $x$-axis
with a velocity whose direction makes an angle $\theta$ with $x$-axis such that $\theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ or $\theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)$
with a velocity of magnitude $\frac{m_1}{2 m_2} v \sqrt{5}$

solution.text:
before collision
After collision
$\begin{aligned} & \rightarrow v_x=\frac{m_2 v}{m_1} \quad v_y=\frac{m_2 v}{2 m_1} \\ & v=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2} v\left(\frac{m_2}{m_1}\right) \\ & \rightarrow \tan \theta=\frac{v_y}{v_x}\left(\frac{1}{2} \text { or }-\frac{1}{2}\right) \quad \text { (As per choice of original direction) } \\ & \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \text { or } \tan ^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \end{aligned}$
